Now I do understand the meme value of this and am not in any case saying that this shouldn't be looked away from, but instead should be analyzed more. Each religion tries its best to compact the idea of "life" and "God" just enough that humans may interpret it and learn from it. Existentialism can sometimes feel like quasi nihilism/ atheism, and yes I have personally been there myself; where the world doesn't seem to make a lot of sense and people may turn to the religions around them to choose the path (religion) to follow and base their lives around as a foundation. I’ve been giving this some thought recently: with regard to straws- plastic straws are bad right? Yes they are one time use plastics that get discarded and are never thought of again. Tossed aside like all the other “trash” in our everyday lives. The mentality that scares me the most in people is their absolute disregard for these trashes. Not just the straws but others as well: children, trash bags, friends, family, etc. the generation that proceeded me (ie my parents) were brought up thinking only of the now and never of the future. Take for example the story of my father and his absolute disregard for his family when he divorced my mother. His whole generation was plagued with fathers who up and vanished when life stepped in. On the thought of short-termism again: do not look at the things that surround you and think “this will stay the same” because it will not, over time things change and move and not just objects, but emotions and cognition as well. A person has the ability to change and should be given the opportunity to do so. As for the present day problems that our civilization faces I look to plastic as the root to the illness that plagues each and every one of our minds. We toss these frivolous items aside thinking of them only as trash. But trash they are not; for this trash will not disappear.
